Looking at the graph, the two rising dose‑response curves (filled black circles and open red squares) correspond to the two catecholamines. At a concentration of 30 µM (3 × 10⁻⁵ M), the black curve is at roughly 1.3–1.4 relative fluorescence while the red curve is at roughly 1.1–1.2. The error bars at this region are small and do not overlap, so the separation between the two curves is larger than the experimental uncertainty. Therefore the difference between the responses to norepinephrine and epinephrine at 30 µM is statistically significant.

[ANSWER]B[/ANSWER]
